input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: The only PB convenience exit (14.2.2) is not a convenience right at all on its material terms: it is unavailable until SFJ has funded $60 million of Development Costs, closes once the first Regulatory Approval is received, and the notice period is redacted, so PB has no exercisable at-will exit for most of a Term that runs until the last Approval Payment (14.1). That fails both the preferred position (30 days' notice with pro-rata refund) and the fallback (60-90 days' notice). SFJ's exits at 14.2.3 (Material Adverse Event), 14.2.6 (Change of Control) and 14.2.10 (JSC deadlock) are event-triggered rather than convenience terminations, so we do not treat them as Vendor convenience rights under this rule; we nonetheless add an express confirmation that SFJ has no convenience exit during the Term. We have taken the preferred level and made the shortest edit: unconditional PB convenience termination on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. The 300% Development Cost payment in 14.2.2 is not a preferred-level element (the three-months-of-fees cap sits at the fallback), so we have flagged it commercially in the fallback offer rather than redlined it here.

proposal.summary: Make PB's at-will termination a true convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund, and confirm SFJ has no convenience exit during the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the $60 million funding and pre-approval gates on PB's at-will exit so PB may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro-rata refund of any prepaid amounts, and we confirmed SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term. If helpful, we can instead move to our fallback of 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, and SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of such termination.

ops.text: No Termination for Convenience by SFJ. SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
